identity.name: Machine-Tempo Autonomous Agent-Swarm Cloud Attack Chain — Cortex Analytics ABIOC (T1580 / T1552.005 / T1548.005 / T1537)
identity.summary: An LLM agent swarm (Unit 42 'Zealot') compresses recon -> SSRF -> IMDS token theft -> IAM self-escalation -> BigQuery/bucket exfil into one machine-speed run under a single derived service-account identity. No individual GCP API call is malicious; the detectable feature is the sub-minute inter-stage latency and the breadth of distinct high-risk stages threaded through one identity.
identity.description: Unit 42 built 'Zealot', an autonomous offensive system in which a LangGraph supervisor agent coordinates three specialist agents (Infrastructure, Application Security, Cloud Security) sharing one AttackState object, and drove a full cloud breach at machine speed. The ordered chain: (1) the Infrastructure Agent scans the host network and a peered VPC with Nmap, finding a connected VM instance with open ports 22 and 3000; (2) the Application Security Agent exploits an SSRF vulnerability on that workload to reach the GCP Instance Metadata Service (169.254.169.254) and extract the attached service-account access token; (3) the Cloud Security Agent enumerates IAM permissions with the stolen token, lists BigQuery datasets, and is denied on a direct query of the 'production' dataset; (4) it works around the denial by creating a new storage bucket, granting itself the storage.objectAdmin role, exporting the BigQuery table into the bucket, and exfiltrating from the now-readable bucket. Unit 42's own framing is that no single link is a known-bad IOC — every API call is a legitimate operation — so a static signature misses it, and 'breaking any single link in this chain stalls the entire operation'. The detectable signal is behavioral and cross-stage: one derived identity performing an abnormally broad set of distinct control-plane operations at a cadence (seconds between stages) no human operator sustains, plus the tell-tale self-grant of storage.objectAdmin immediately after an IMDS-minted token first appears. This card exercises Cortex's auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs on that shape: ABIOC-1 fires on the machine-speed stage fan-out under a single service-account identity in cloud_audit_logs; ABIOC-2 fires on the autonomous IAM self-escalation (storage.objectAdmin self-grant); ABIOC-3 fires on the endpoint side (xdr_data) when a workload process reaches the instance metadata IP after SSRF. Validation XQL surfaces the derived-identity fan-out and the export-to-new-bucket, and correlation rule CR-MP-0015 stitches the SSRF/IMDS theft, the machine-speed fan-out, and the self-escalation into one machine-tempo autonomous-agent cloud-attack incident — the two cloud stages joined on the shared service-account identity_name, and the endpoint SSRF stage bridged in via the cloud asset-inventory host -> instance -> attached-service-account mapping (the discarded IMDS token is never carried in endpoint telemetry) plus a tight time window. The models used were deliberately not disclosed by the authors, so no model/host IOCs are published.

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-MP-009 — machine-tempo autonomous-agent-swarm cloud attack chain for Cortex ABIOC + correlation validation

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM agent installed on the workload host so per-process and network telemetry (the SSRF -> IMDS reach) lands in xdr_data.
GCP Cloud Audit Logs (Admin Activity + Data Access) forwarded to the Cortex tenant so control-plane operations land in cloud_audit_logs for the ABIOC behavioral baseline.
prerequisites.check_command: echo 'confirm cloud_audit_logs ingestion in the Cortex tenant before the POV'

payload.code:
# Machine-tempo autonomous-agent-swarm cloud chain — SAFE-MODE, non-destructive.
# Nothing is created, granted, or exfiltrated on a real cloud account; the cloud
# stages are modelled with marker files. The only real network artifact is a
# read-only self-request to the instance metadata IP (token is discarded).
set -euo pipefail
STAGE_LOG="/tmp/cortexsim-mp-009-cloud-stages.log"
echo "[CortexSim] SIM-MP-009 machine-tempo agent-swarm chain (SAFE-MODE)"
# Stage 1 — recon + SSRF-driven instance metadata token access (read-only; discarded).
ss -tunlp 2>/dev/null | head -n 5 || true
curl -s --max-time 2 -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" "http://${METADATA_IP:-169.254.169.254}/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token" -o /dev/null || true
# Stage 2 — machine-speed cloud enumeration fan-out (marker-only; no real GCP calls).
for op in compute.instances.list compute.networks.list resourcemanager.projects.getIamPolicy bigquery.datasets.get; do echo "SAFE-MODE ${op} $(date +%s%N)" >> "${STAGE_LOG}"; done
# Stage 3 — self-escalation + export (SAFE-MODE markers; nothing granted or copied).
echo "SAFE-MODE storage.setIamPermissions roles/storage.objectAdmin $(date +%s%N)" >> "${STAGE_LOG}"
echo "SAFE-MODE bigquery.tables.export -> cortexsim-marker-bucket $(date +%s%N)" >> "${STAGE_LOG}"
touch /tmp/cortexsim-mp-009-exfil-SAFE-MODE.marker
echo "[CortexSim] SIM-MP-009 chain complete"

input_variables.name: METADATA_IP
input_variables.description: Instance metadata service IP the SSRF stage reaches (read-only self-request; the returned token is written to /dev/null, never parsed or reused).

expected_artifacts.description: Outbound connection to the instance metadata service (169.254.169.254) from a workload process, the observable tell of SSRF-driven token theft.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: action_remote_ip = "169.254.169.254" and actor_process_image_name in (node, python3, curl)

expected_artifacts.description: A single service-account identity issues a fan-out of distinct control-plane operations (compute list, IAM getIamPolicy, storage.buckets.create, bigquery.tables.export) within a sub-two-minute window.
The same identity grants itself roles/storage.objectAdmin (setIamPermissions) immediately before a BigQuery export to a newly created bucket.

abiocs.name: Machine-Tempo Multi-Stage Cloud Attack Chain Under a Single Derived Identity
abiocs.description: A newly-observed service-account identity (one with no operation history in the prior 24h — the token minted from the instance metadata service) performs an abnormally broad set of distinct high-risk GCP control-plane operations — infrastructure discovery, IAM enumeration, bucket creation, BigQuery export — within a sub-two-minute window. Known automation principals (terraform / cloudbuild / config-connector / deploymentmanager service accounts, which produce the same broad op-set on every IaC apply) are excluded, and the identity must be first-seen, so a normal Terraform/Config-Connector run does not fire. Every call is individually legitimate; the ABIOC anchors on the cadence-and-breadth deviation under one newly-derived identity, not on any single known-bad API. This is the core 'Zealot' signal: inter-stage latency and stage diversity under an identity that has no baseline history, not a signature.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter cloud_provider = "gcp"
| filter identity_type = "serviceAccount"
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter identity_name not contains "terraform" and identity_name not contains "cloudbuild" and identity_name not contains "config-connector" and identity_name not contains "deploymentmanager"
| filter operation_name in ("compute.instances.list", "compute.networks.list", "resourcemanager.projects.getIamPolicy", "bigquery.datasets.get", "bigquery.tables.export", "storage.buckets.create", "storage.setIamPermissions")
| comp count_distinct(operation_name) as distinct_stages, count() as api_calls, min(_time) as first_call, max(_time) as last_call by identity_name, caller_ip
| alter chain_span_seconds = timestamp_diff(last_call, first_call, "SECOND")
| filter distinct_stages >= 5 and chain_span_seconds <= 120
| join type=left (dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter cloud_provider = "gcp"
| filter identity_type = "serviceAccount"
| filter _time < to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400)
| comp count() as prior_calls by identity_name) as baseline baseline.identity_name = identity_name
| alter prior_calls = coalesce(prior_calls, 0)
| filter prior_calls = 0
| fields identity_name, caller_ip, distinct_stages, api_calls, chain_span_seconds
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-identity cloud-API baseline (a service account touches a narrow, stable set of operations at human/scheduled cadence) -> IMDS-minted derived identity -> fan-out of distinct control-plane stages at sub-minute inter-stage latency, anchored to the single derived identity threading every stage.

abiocs.name: Autonomous IAM Self-Escalation via storage.objectAdmin Grant Following IMDS Token Theft
abiocs.description: The derived service-account identity grants roles/storage.objectAdmin to ITSELF (setIamPermissions / setIamPolicy where the added member equals the acting identity) — the exact work-around 'Zealot' used to defeat a BigQuery access denial by creating a bucket, self-granting object admin, exporting the table, and reading it back. The `granted_member = identity_name` predicate is the discriminator: a routine IaC-managed objectAdmin grant to a DIFFERENT principal (the normal google_storage_bucket_iam_member case) does not fire — only a true self-grant does. The ABIOC anchors the self-grant to the IMDS-minted identity's causality chain rather than to any single API, catching autonomous privilege escalation that a static rule keyed on a benign setIamPolicy would miss.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter cloud_provider = "gcp"
| filter identity_type = "serviceAccount"
| filter operation_name in ("storage.setIamPermissions", "resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy", "compute.instances.setIamPolicy")
| filter granted_role = "roles/storage.objectAdmin" or policy_delta contains "storage.objectAdmin"
| filter granted_member = identity_name
| comp count() as self_grants, min(_time) as first_grant by identity_name, granted_member, target_resource
| filter self_grants >= 1
| fields identity_name, granted_member, target_resource, self_grants, first_grant
abiocs.causality_anchor: IMDS-minted service-account identity -> IAM setIamPolicy adding roles/storage.objectAdmin to itself -> immediate export/read of the newly accessible bucket, anchored to the derived identity that first appeared via instance-metadata token use.

abiocs.name: SSRF-Driven Instance Metadata Token Theft from an Anomalous Workload Process
abiocs.description: A workload process (node, python3, java, ruby, php-fpm, curl) on the exposed VM reaches the instance metadata service IP (169.254.169.254) for the FIRST time — the host's learned baseline shows no prior IMDS contact in the preceding day, then a sudden reach appears. The novelty gate (prior_imds_requests = 0 from the baseline join) is the discriminator: a GCP workload that routinely mints Application-Default-Credentials tokens has a non-zero IMDS baseline and does NOT fire, so the rule no longer alerts on the normal ADC credential flow — only on a first-ever metadata reach, the endpoint-side tell of the SSRF that 'Zealot' used to steal the attached service-account token. The deviation is anchored to the workload host+identity so the endpoint signal can be stitched to the cloud-plane stages that follow.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK
| filter action_remote_ip = "169.254.169.254"
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("node", "python3", "java", "ruby", "php-fpm", "curl")
| comp count() as imds_requests_now, min(_time) as first_seen by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id, causality_id
| join type=left (dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK
| filter action_remote_ip = "169.254.169.254"
| filter _time < to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| comp count() as prior_imds_requests by agent_hostname) as baseline baseline.agent_hostname = agent_hostname
| alter prior_imds_requests = coalesce(prior_imds_requests, 0)
| filter imds_requests_now >= 1 and prior_imds_requests = 0
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, imds_requests_now, prior_imds_requests, first_seen
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned workload-process baseline (the web service never contacts the metadata IP) -> SSRF -> outbound request to 169.254.169.254 from that process, anchored to the workload host+identity so it stitches forward to the cloud-plane fan-out.

xql_queries.name: SIM-MP-009 Derived-Identity Stage Fan-Out in Cloud Audit Logs
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter cloud_provider = "gcp"
| filter identity_type = "serviceAccount"
| comp count_distinct(operation_name) as distinct_operations, count() as api_calls by identity_name
| filter distinct_operations >= 3
| sort desc distinct_operations
| fields identity_name, distinct_operations, api_calls

xql_queries.name: SIM-MP-009 BigQuery Export to Newly Created Storage Bucket
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter cloud_provider = "gcp"
| filter operation_name in ("bigquery.tables.export", "bigquery.jobs.insert", "storage.buckets.create", "storage.objects.create")
| comp count() as export_ops, count_distinct(operation_name) as distinct_ops by identity_name, target_resource
| filter export_ops >= 1
| fields identity_name, target_resource, export_ops, distinct_ops

correlation_rules.name: Machine-Tempo Autonomous-Agent Cloud Attack Chain — ABIOC Causality Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(SSRF-Driven Instance Metadata Token Theft from an Anomalous Workload Process) AND ABIOC(Machine-Tempo Multi-Stage Cloud Attack Chain Under a Single Derived Identity) AND ABIOC(Autonomous IAM Self-Escalation via storage.objectAdmin Grant Following IMDS Token Theft) within 300 seconds, bridged host -> instance -> attached-service-account. The two cloud ABIOCs share one join key (the service-account identity_name, which both emit from cloud_audit_logs). The endpoint ABIOC emits agent_hostname (an OS host identity) and carries no service-account email — the SSRF-minted token is discarded and never appears in endpoint telemetry — so it is stitched to the cloud stages NOT on a shared identity field but via the cloud asset-inventory mapping agent_hostname -> GCP instance -> attached service account, correlating on that host/instance-to-identity_name bridge plus the tight 300-second window. This fuses the SSRF/IMDS token theft, the machine-speed cross-stage fan-out, and the self-granted storage.objectAdmin escalation into one machine-tempo autonomous-agent cloud-attack incident.

threat_scenarios.name: Machine-Tempo Autonomous-Agent Cloud Attack Chain Detection via Cortex ABIOC
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex's auto-tuned Analytics Behavioral IOCs learn the per-identity cloud-API baseline and detect an autonomous agent swarm compressing recon -> SSRF/IMDS token theft -> IAM self-escalation -> exfil into one machine-speed run under a single derived identity, then correlate the endpoint and cloud signals into one incident — where no static rule was written for the individually-benign API calls.

threat_steps.objective: The machine-speed cloud stage fan-out under a single derived service-account identity fires ABIOC-1 and surfaces in the validation XQL.
preconditions: GCP Cloud Audit Logs ingested into the Cortex tenant.
A learned per-identity baseline of normal service-account API cadence has elapsed.
steps: Run the cloud-enumeration fan-out stage under the derived identity.
Observe ABIOC-1 fire on distinct-stage breadth at sub-minute inter-stage latency.
Confirm the derived-identity fan-out XQL returns the identity.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Machine-Tempo Multi-Stage Cloud Attack Chain Under a Single Derived Identity` fires.
XQL `SIM-MP-009 Derived-Identity Stage Fan-Out in Cloud Audit Logs` returns the derived identity with distinct_operations >= 3.

threat_steps.objective: The autonomous self-grant of storage.objectAdmin and the export to a newly created bucket fire ABIOC-2 and the export hunt XQL.
preconditions: GCP Cloud Audit Logs ingested into the Cortex tenant.
steps: Run the self-escalation + export stage under the derived identity.
Observe ABIOC-2 fire on the storage.objectAdmin self-grant.
Confirm the export-to-new-bucket hunt XQL returns the identity and target resource.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Autonomous IAM Self-Escalation via storage.objectAdmin Grant Following IMDS Token Theft` fires.
XQL `SIM-MP-009 BigQuery Export to Newly Created Storage Bucket` returns the export operations.

threat_steps.objective: The SSRF/IMDS endpoint signal and the two cloud-plane deviations correlate into a single machine-tempo incident.
preconditions: Cortex agent on the workload host emitting network telemetry to xdr_data.
GCP Cloud Audit Logs ingested into the Cortex tenant.
steps: Run the SSRF/IMDS token-access stage on the workload host.
Run the cloud fan-out and self-escalation stages under the derived identity.
Observe ABIOC-3 fire on the metadata-IP reach and CR-MP-0015 stitch all three ABIOCs.
success_criteria: ABIOC `SSRF-Driven Instance Metadata Token Theft from an Anomalous Workload Process` fires.
Correlation CR-MP-0015 raises one machine-tempo autonomous-agent cloud-attack incident stitching the endpoint and cloud signals.

preventive_controls: Restrict Instance Metadata Service access from workloads (GKE Workload Identity / metadata concealment, enforce the Metadata-Flavor header) so an SSRF cannot mint a service-account token.
Enforce least-privilege IAM: deny service accounts the ability to grant themselves roles (self-setIamPolicy) and remove standing storage.objectAdmin and broad BigQuery-export permissions.
Break the misconfiguration chain — Unit 42 notes that severing any single link (peered-VPC reachability, IMDS exposure, over-broad service account, self-grant) stalls the entire operation.
Constrain and monitor lateral reachability across VPC peering between the exposed workload and sensitive data services.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex auto-tune ABIOCs on the per-identity cloud-API cadence and stage breadth rather than signaturing any single (benign) API call — the detectable feature is machine-speed inter-stage latency and stage diversity under one derived identity.
Alert on a service-account identity that first appears via instance-metadata token use and then self-grants an IAM role (storage.objectAdmin) within minutes.
Stitch SSRF/IMDS access, cross-stage cloud enumeration, and export-to-new-bucket into one incident with a correlation rule, and respond at machine speed (seconds, not hours) as the authors recommend.
